newsitem.title: USA: CBOT Nov soybean expiration seen buoying market.
newsitem.headline: CBOT Nov soybean expiration seen buoying market.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures early Tuesday will find support from the liquidation of shorts in the November contract as that month nears expiration at 1201 CST, traders said.
"There are a bunch of little guys in there who have overextended their welcome, there are no majors," a trader said.
November late Monday rallied as shorts bailed out of that month and the open interest dropped a hefty ten million bushels during Monday's session, according to CBOT records.
The open interest in the November early Tuesday stood at a more "comfortable" level for an expiration day at three million bushels.

November Tuesday ended at $7.11-1/4 per bushel, up 12-1/4 cents and other months closed one to 6-1/2 cents per bushel higher. November, in CBOT's Project A overnight trading, closed at $7.14-3/4, up 3-1/2 cents from Monday's close.

"Three million isn't a lot but they still have to get out of there so it could be interesting," a trader said. "The only ones who should be in there on expiration day should be the big guys (commercials) who want to take the grain and they're not there."
